_meta.indication: NUZYRA is a tetracycline-class antibacterial indicated in adults for community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP) and acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) caused by susceptible microorganisms

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study ABSI-1108, IV-to-oral omadacycline in ABSSSI
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active-controlled non-inferiority trial comparing omadacycline to linezolid (NI margin 10%), IV-to-oral switch
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) due to susceptible Gram-positive pathogens
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical success at the early clinical response (ECR) timepoint, defined as ≥ 20% reduction in lesion size in the mITT population 48-72 hours after first dose
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical success at ECR: 84.8% (268/316) omadacycline vs 85.5% (266/311) linezolid; treatment difference -0.7% (95% CI -6.3, 4.9) — noninferior

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study ABSI-16301, oral-only omadacycline in ABSSSI
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1), double-blind, double-dummy, active comparator-controlled Phase 3 non-inferiority trial of oral omadacycline vs oral linezolid
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with ABSSSI known or suspected to be due to a Gram-positive pathogen
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical success at ECR, ≥ 20% reduction in lesion size in the mITT population within 48-72 hours after first dose
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical success at ECR: 87.5% (315/360) omadacycline vs 82.5% (297/360) linezolid; treatment difference 5.0 (95% CI -0.2, 10.3) — noninferior

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study CABP-1200, omadacycline vs moxifloxacin in CABP
pivotal_trials.design: Single randomized, active-controlled non-inferiority trial comparing omadacycline to moxifloxacin (NI margin 10%)
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (~60% PORT Risk Class III, ~26% PORT Risk Class IV)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical success at early clinical response (ECR), 72 to 120 hours after first dose, based on 4 symptoms (cough, sputum production, pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea)
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical success at ECR: 81.1% (313/386) omadacycline vs 82.7% (321/388) moxifloxacin; treatment difference -1.6 (95% CI -7.1, 3.8) — noninferior

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥2%): nausea, vomiting, infusion site reactions, ALT/AST/GGT increased, hypertension, headache, diarrhea, insomnia, constipation. In pooled ABSSSI trials nausea 21.9% (vs 8.7% linezolid) and vomiting 11.4% (vs 3.9%). A mortality imbalance was observed in the CABP trial (30-day all-cause mortality 8 [2.1%] omadacycline vs 3 [0.8%] moxifloxacin).
target_moa: Omadacycline is a semi-synthetic tetracycline-class antibacterial; tetracyclines bind the bacterial ribosome 30S subunit and inhibit binding of aminoacyl-tRNA, blocking bacterial protein synthesis

advisory_committee.vote: AMDAC met August 8, 2018. ABSSSI: 17 voted yes, 1 no. CABP: 14 voted yes, 4 no.

summary.text: NUZYRA received QIDP designation and Fast Track Designation for CABP/ABSSSI, and as such received priority review; the application was submitted and received February 02, 2018 and approved first cycle October 02, 2018 following an AMDAC advisory committee meeting. Approval was based on adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials, not accelerated approval.

citations.quote: 3487-4 Conduct an active-controlled safety and efficacy study in adults with community-acquired bacterial pneumonia

We have determined that an analysis of spontaneous postmarketing adverse events reported under subsection 505(k)(1) of the FDCA will not be sufficient to identify the serious risk of mortality imbalance in patients with CABP and the development of resistance to NUZYRA (omadacycline) in microorganisms specific to the CABP and ABSSSI indications in the label.
